query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these travel-expense records.

per_column.name: is_processed
per_column.rationale: A binary flag derived from presence/absence of processed_date (nan -> 0). It is well-grounded and offers a usable grouping axis (processed vs not), but it is largely a restatement of whether processed_date exists, so its analytical leverage is modest.

per_column.name: days_to_process
per_column.rationale: Elapsed days between opening and processing is a genuinely useful new axis for spotting delays/outliers. However for unprocessed rows (nan processed_date) it invents large specific values (e.g. 970, 965, 1051) rather than leaving them unknown, asserting a concrete duration the source does not support. This partially contradicts the is_processed=0 rows.

per_column.name: amount_decile
per_column.rationale: Deciles of the existing amount column give a clean, uniform banding (50 per bin) that supports grouping and comparison of spend levels. It is a sound transformation of a present numeric column; the decile values are derivable, though the sample lacks amount to fully verify.

judge.rationale: The added columns provide reasonable new axes (spend banding, processing latency, processed flag) for exploring travel-expense records. amount_decile and is_processed are well-grounded transformations of existing fields; days_to_process is the most analytically valuable but injects fabricated large durations for rows with missing processed_date instead of marking them unknown, which lowers overall groundedness. No completeness penalty applied.
